neighbours.label: particle or verb of getting out of or away from a place or burden ('got out', 'ran off', 'stripped of', 'light loads'): fires on the departure/release word; the same scenes where the actor stays put stay low
fire: At the gas station, the woman got out of her car to stretch her legs.
As soon as the alarm rang, the boys ran off down the alley.
Once the bus stopped, an old man climbed out through the back door.
During the robbery, the thief slipped out of the shop unnoticed.
After the flood, the house was stripped of its carpets and plaster.
Late at night the cat crept out of the barn and vanished.
Startled by the noise, the horse bolted off across the field.
When the rain stopped, the hikers got out of the tent and packed up.
quiet: At the gas station, the woman stayed in her car and checked her phone.
As soon as the alarm rang, the boys sat quietly at their desks.
Once the bus stopped, an old man waited patiently in his seat.
During the robbery, the clerk remained calm behind the counter.
After the flood, the house was painted a bright shade of yellow.
Late at night the cat slept soundly on the warm blanket.
Startled by the noise, the horse stood still and raised its head.
When the rain stopped, the hikers sat in the tent and drank tea.

short: getting out / away (got out, ran off)
